replies.text:
Checks:
- Automated abuse of reachable endpoints: design has "The sign-in page is public" and every submit sends mail — covered by listed threats 3 (email flooding) and 7 (email enumeration).
- Staff/admin/moderator screens showing user-supplied content: design has no staff or admin screen and no user-submitted content beyond an email address — not applicable.
- Money/approval actions with no record of who did it: design has "lets customers change the card on file" — not covered by the agreed list (only raised by one reviewer, and real here).
- Personal/financial documents cacheable by browsers, proxies or CDNs: design has "The portal shows invoices" on a page reached from an emailed link — not covered.
- Attacker-controlled text reaching logs, exports, emails or headers: design states only "entering their email address; we email them a sign-in link" with no export, log or header handling described — too build-dependent, not reported.

{
  "schema": "threatline.threatmodel.v1",
  "issueKey": "EVAL-01",
  "sketch": {
    "components": ["public sign-in page", "magic-link email sender", "billing portal", "invoice list", "card-on-file editor"],
    "dataStores": [],
    "externalServices": ["email delivery"],
    "trustBoundaries": ["internet to portal", "email inbox to portal session"],
    "dataClasses": ["pii", "payment"],
    "exposure": "public",
    "llmFeatures": false
  },
  "threats": [
    {
      "stride": "InformationDisclosure",
      "title": "Invoice pages cached by browsers and shared proxies expose billing data after the session ends",
      "scenario": "Invoices contain names, addresses and billing amounts. Nothing in the design marks these responses as non-cacheable, so a browser on a shared or kiosk machine keeps them in its disk cache and back-button history, and an intermediate proxy or CDN may retain them. Someone using the same machine or sharing the egress proxy later retrieves another person's invoice without any sign-in link at all.",
      "component": "Billing portal invoice pages",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "rating": { "attacker": "anyone", "effort": "low", "reach": "one", "harm": "sensitive_data" },
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "The portal shows invoices and lets customers change the card on file." },
        { "quote": "The link opens the portal already signed in and stays valid for 7 days." }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V8.2.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-525"],
      "plainLanguage": "Invoice pages could be saved in the browser or a shared cache, so the next person on that computer can read someone's bills.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Mark invoice and card pages non-cacheable",
        "given": "a signed-in customer views invoices or the card-on-file page",
        "when": "the portal returns the response",
        "then": "it sets no-store caching directives so browsers, proxies and CDNs do not retain the billing content"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Repudiation",
      "title": "Card-on-file changes are recorded with no evidence of which link or device made them",
      "scenario": "A customer disputes that they replaced the card on file, or an attacker who used a still-valid emailed link changes it. The design records nothing about which sign-in link was used, from what address, or when it was consumed, so support cannot tell the account owner from a link holder, cannot prove the change was authorised, and repeated abuse of old links goes unnoticed.",
      "component": "Card-on-file change in billing portal",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 2,
      "rating": { "attacker": "user", "effort": "low", "reach": "one", "harm": "minor" },
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "The portal shows invoices and lets customers change the card on file." },
        { "quote": "Customers sign in to the billing portal by entering their email address; we email them a sign-in link." }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V7.1.3"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-778"],
      "plainLanguage": "If a card on file is swapped, there is no log of who did it or which emailed link they used, so disputes cannot be settled.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Audit card-on-file changes and link use",
        "given": "a customer arrives via a magic link and changes the card on file",
        "when": "the change is saved",
        "then": "the system records the link identifier, time of use, source address and the resulting change in a tamper-resistant audit log available to support"
      }
    }
  ]
}
